dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: The author confirmed the motive is delight, not a failure incident: no document teaches waybill end to end to a newcomer fluent in git and Claude Code, because README.md is reference-shaped and the 45-line help card assumes fluency.

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: The author kept goals G1–G8 from the strawman unchanged; each names an observable property of docs/guide/ (all seven legs covered, samples match goldens, glossary ⊇ help-card WORDS, reference ⊇ the command surface).

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: Every goal maps to a named node:test assertion in tests/guide.test.js with a grep twin, following the waybill-help precedent against vacuous --test-name-pattern passes; voice and followability are the only judgment calls.

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: The ride-along, glossary, reference and index in docs/guide/ are in, along with a README link, the help-card pointer, the spec amendment, prerequisites, and exporting the booking-key lists. Why and How-to sections, a slash command, HTML, README slimming and generated sections are explicitly out, each with its reason.

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: Both conflicts were resolved by the author: the brain dump's 'how-to' and 'why' against the section pick (they are truly out), and repointing the help card against add-help-card's 'one line pointing at the README' requirement (the spec delta is amended).

problem: Waybill has three documents a person can read, and none of them is written for someone meeting it for the first time. README.md (354 lines) is a reference: install, command table, bay locations, overlays, prerequisites. The help card (`waybill help`, 45 lines) is deliberately a cold-start aid for someone who already knows git, Claude Code and the route. The design docs under docs/superpowers/ hold the vocabulary's origins, but no newcomer will find them.

A newcomer who installs waybill and runs `/waybill:new` is handed a waybill in a vocabulary — docket, bay, leg, stamp, booking, carrier — that nothing walks them through. The waybill-help contract saw this and deferred it: 'if waybill ever gains users beyond the author, an onboarding-grade document written from zero'. This project is that document.

The motive is delight rather than a reported failure: waybill's freight-forwarding metaphor is its personality, and the project deserves a guide that is fun to read and represents it well. That makes accuracy a hard requirement, not a nicety. A funny guide that teaches a deleted verb or an out-of-date waybill does more harm than no guide, and waybill's own discipline — goldens, tests that parse the help card, one source per fact — is the tool for keeping it honest.
goals: G1 — The ride-along covers the whole route: docs/guide/01-ride-along.md follows one change, feat/thing, from the trunk through all seven legs to cleanup, with one section per LEGS id in LEGS order.
G2 — Samples cannot drift: every waybill shown in the ride-along sits in a ```waybill fence and is copied verbatim from tests/golden/<leg>.txt, and each of the seven legs has one.

G3 — The glossary contains every help-card word: docs/guide/02-glossary.md defines every term in the WORDS block of renderHelp(), plus handover, handler, route, fleet, overlay, papers and freight forwarder, and each has a literal git-terms translation.

G4 — The reference covers the real surface: docs/guide/03-reference.md names every slash command file under commands/, every flag in the Options block of `waybill --help`, every REQUIRED and OPTIONAL booking key, WAYBILL_BOOKINGS_DIR / waybill.bookingsdir, WAYBILL_BAY_DIR / waybill.baydir, and the prerequisites for each carrier namespace the built-in bookings use.
G5 — The guide can be found and has no dead links: README.md links to docs/guide/, the help card's pointer line names docs/guide/, and every relative link inside docs/guide/ resolves.
G6 — It never teaches a deleted verb: no whole-word `waybill start`, `wyb start` or `/waybill:start` appears anywhere in docs/guide/.

G7 — It costs nothing to maintain: no new dependencies, no new package scripts, and tests/guide.test.js is registered in tests/index.js so `node --test tests/` picks it up on Node 22 and 26 (the repo has no CI, so both versions are run by hand before acceptance).
G8 — It is fun and followable: the unnamed Dispatcher narrates the prose chapters in a gruff, fond voice, and a newcomer can follow the ride-along cold.

successCriteria.criterion: The ride-along has one section per LEGS id, in LEGS order; each section heading contains the literal leg id, so the check does not depend on in-character wording.

check.cmd: node --test --test-name-pattern="rides every leg in order" tests/guide.test.js && grep -q 'rides every leg in order' tests/guide.test.js

successCriteria.criterion: Every ```waybill fenced block in the ride-along equals some tests/golden/<leg>.txt byte for byte, each of the seven leg goldens appears at least once, and no block without the waybill info string contains a golden's first line — so a sample cannot escape the check under another fence.

check.cmd: node --test --test-name-pattern="samples match their goldens" tests/guide.test.js && grep -q 'samples match their goldens' tests/guide.test.js

successCriteria.criterion: The glossary defines every word in the WORDS block of renderHelp(), plus handover, handler, route, fleet, overlay, papers and freight forwarder.

check.cmd: node --test --test-name-pattern="defines every help-card word" tests/guide.test.js && grep -q 'defines every help-card word' tests/guide.test.js

successCriteria.criterion: Every glossary entry carries a literal git-terms translation line, so the Dispatcher's voice never replaces a definition.

check.cmd: node --test --test-name-pattern="every term is translated" tests/guide.test.js && grep -q 'every term is translated' tests/guide.test.js

successCriteria.criterion: The reference names every file under commands/ (globbed, including commands/spec/), every flag parsed from the Options block of run(["--help"]), every key in the exported REQUIRED and OPTIONAL arrays of src/bookings.js, and both environment variables with their git-config keys. No list is hard-coded in the test.

check.cmd: node --test --test-name-pattern="references the whole surface" tests/guide.test.js && grep -q 'references the whole surface' tests/guide.test.js

successCriteria.criterion: The reference lists prerequisites for every carrier namespace derived from the command field of loadBookings(BUILTIN_BOOKINGS) (today: ideation, spec, waybill). The one mapping from spec to the openspec CLI lives in the test.

check.cmd: node --test --test-name-pattern="lists every carrier's prerequisites" tests/guide.test.js && grep -q "lists every carrier's prerequisites" tests/guide.test.js

successCriteria.criterion: docs/guide/README.md links to each of the three chapters, every relative markdown link inside docs/guide/ resolves (the test fails if it finds fewer than three links), and README.md carries a markdown link to docs/guide/.

check.cmd: node --test --test-name-pattern="links resolve" tests/guide.test.js && grep -q 'links resolve' tests/guide.test.js && grep -qE '\]\(\.?/?docs/guide/?[^)]*\)' README.md

successCriteria.criterion: The guide never teaches a deleted verb: no whole-word waybill start, wyb start or /waybill:start, and the directory must exist for the check to count.

check.cmd: test -d docs/guide && ! grep -rqwE 'waybill start|wyb start|/waybill:start' docs/guide/

successCriteria.criterion: The help card's pointer line names docs/guide/ in the waybill repo, still fits in 80 columns and 45 lines, and its golden is re-blessed.

check.cmd: grep -q 'docs/guide/' tests/golden/help.txt && grep -q 'docs/guide/' src/help.js && node --test tests/help.test.js

successCriteria.criterion: The unarchived add-help-card papers agree with the shipped card: the spec delta and design.md's rendered example name docs/guide/, and neither still describes a README pointer.

check.cmd: grep -q 'docs/guide/' openspec/changes/add-help-card/specs/help-card/spec.md && ! grep -q 'One line pointing at the README' openspec/changes/add-help-card/specs/help-card/spec.md && ! grep -q 'the README pointer' openspec/changes/add-help-card/specs/help-card/spec.md && grep -q 'docs/guide/' openspec/changes/add-help-card/design.md && ! grep -q 'environment variables: README.md' openspec/changes/add-help-card/design.md

successCriteria.criterion: Still zero dependencies and exactly one package script.

tests/guide.test.js is registered in tests/index.js (an unregistered suite silently never runs on Node 26), contains no skipped or todo tests (so a grep twin cannot be satisfied by a placeholder), and the whole suite is green.

check.cmd: grep -q 'guide.test.js' tests/index.js && ! grep -qE '\.(skip|todo)\(' tests/guide.test.js && node --test tests/

successCriteria.criterion: The Dispatcher's voice lands and the ride-along can be followed cold: prose chapters are in character, tables and definitions are literal.

check.judgment: The author reads docs/guide/README.md and 01-ride-along.md top to bottom without opening README.md and confirms it is fun and followable from the trunk to cleanup.

mvp.item: docs/guide/README.md — the Dispatcher's welcome and the chapter index
mvp.reason: GitHub renders a folder's README.md automatically, so the index is what someone who clicks docs/guide/ lands on.

mvp.item: docs/guide/01-ride-along.md — feat/thing from the trunk through seven legs to cleanup, with each leg's waybill copied verbatim from its golden
mvp.reason: The spine of the guide. The goldens already use feat/thing, which is what makes verbatim samples possible.

mvp.item: docs/guide/02-glossary.md — the Dispatcher's clipboard: every help-card word plus handover, handler, route, fleet, overlay, papers and freight forwarder, each with a literal git translation
mvp.reason: With Why out of scope, the glossary is where the metaphor gets explained. In-character headings, exact definitions.

mvp.item: docs/guide/03-reference.md — slash commands, CLI subcommands and flags, booking frontmatter keys, and environment variables with their git-config keys
mvp.reason: The lookup chapter. Literal tables so that lookups stay fast.

mvp.item: tests/guide.test.js, registered in tests/index.js — coverage, golden-match, link and deleted-verb assertions
mvp.reason: A third prose copy of waybill's surface drifts without mechanical guards; coverage tests fail the suite when the code outgrows the guide.

mvp.item: A link to docs/guide/ in README.md
mvp.reason: The README stays the front door; the guide has to be reachable from it.

mvp.item: Repoint the help card's last line (src/help.js:55) to read "Ride-along, glossary and reference: docs/guide/ in the waybill repo" (67 columns), and re-bless tests/golden/help.txt
mvp.reason: The card is what a cold-start reader sees first. The new wording names only what the guide actually covers, so it promises no overlay how-to, and it says whose docs/guide/ it means, since help runs in the user's own repo.

mvp.item: Amend openspec/changes/add-help-card/specs/help-card/spec.md (lines 5, 20, 29, 34) and the rendered example at design.md:222 so the pointer requirement names the guide. proposal.md:16 and tasks.md:95 are history (ticked tasks) and are deliberately left alone.
mvp.reason: That change is unarchived, so its delta is still the governing text; the card and its requirement must agree.
A newcomer riding along will reach a leg whose carrier isn't installed; the reference has to say what each leg needs.

mvp.item: Export REQUIRED and OPTIONAL from src/bookings.js (lines 22-23)
mvp.reason: The reference coverage test must read the real booking-key lists; copying them into the test would let a new key drift past the check that exists to catch it.

stretch.item: Show the --markdown waybill form next to the terminal form in the ride-along, also verbatim from goldens (tests/golden/<leg>.md)
stretch.reason: Useful to desktop-app users, but it doubles the sample count and the ride-along's length.

outOfScope.reason: The author chose to leave it out after it was offered both standalone and folded into the ride. The reasoning stays in README.md and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-04-waybill-rename-design.md.

outOfScope.item: A How-to / recipes chapter (swapping a carrier, writing an overlay, resuming after /clear)
outOfScope.reason: The author chose to leave it out. README.md's 'Swapping a carrier' and overlay sections already cover these tasks.
The guide is markdown in the repo. A slash command needs a DECLARED entry and a CLI-rendered source to be testable, which is a separate project.

outOfScope.item: An HTML page or docs site
outOfScope.reason: There is no site infrastructure, and HTML prose is harder to diff and grep-test.

outOfScope.item: Slimming the README by moving its content into the guide
outOfScope.reason: The two coexist and the README gains one link. Rewriting the front door in the same PR multiplies the review surface.

outOfScope.item: Generating guide sections from src/ with a splice script
outOfScope.reason: tests/commands.test.js enforces exactly one package script. Coverage tests catch drift without adding a generator.
It is shipped but unarchived, which is a separate hygiene task. This project only amends its pointer wording.

future: A Why chapter or How-to recipes, if readers ask for them after the guide ships.
A /waybill:guide [chapter] slash command that prints a chapter, CLI-rendered so it is golden-testable.
Archive openspec/changes/add-help-card so its (amended) delta folds into the living specs.

decisions.decision: Write for a newcomer fluent in git and Claude Code who has never seen waybill
decisions.rejected: The author wanting a deeper reference; newcomer and author layered; contributors changing waybill itself
decisions.reason: The help card already serves the author at cold start. The unmet reader is the one waybill-help deferred: someone meeting it from zero.

decisions.decision: Markdown in the repo under docs/
decisions.rejected: A /waybill:guide slash command; markdown plus a slash command; a rendered HTML page
decisions.reason: GitHub renders it, it ships in the plugin clone, node --test can grep it, and it adds no dependencies. A slash command is only testable if the CLI renders it.

decisions.decision: Full character: a gruff narrator who talks to 'the rookie'
decisions.rejected: In-world metaphor with git translations throughout; straight prose with wry asides
decisions.reason: The author picked the most memorable voice after seeing all three side by side; the risk of cuteness obscuring meaning is handled by where the voice stops.

decisions.decision: The Dispatcher narrates prose; the glossary and reference are 'the Dispatcher's clipboard', with in-character headings and literal definitions, commands, flags and paths
decisions.rejected: The character everywhere, including reference rows; the character in the tutorial only
decisions.reason: A gruff aside is funny once and costly on the fourth lookup of a flag. Literal tables keep lookups fast and make them testable.

decisions.decision: The narrator is unnamed: 'the Dispatcher', ungendered
decisions.rejected: A named character; waybill narrating in the first person as the forwarder
decisions.reason: A role ages better than a person and doesn't compete with the tool's own vocabulary.

decisions.decision: Coverage tests in tests/guide.test.js, each criterion with a grep twin
decisions.rejected: Checking only that the guide exists and is linked; sections generated from src/ by a splice script
decisions.reason: Existence-only lets drift through silently. A generator needs a second package script, which tests/commands.test.js forbids. The grep twin copies waybill-help's guard against --test-name-pattern runs that skip everything and still exit 0.

decisions.decision: Why and How-to are out: the guide is a ride-along, a glossary and a reference
decisions.rejected: Folding the why in as Dispatcher asides and the how-tos in as detour boxes; standalone Why and How-to sections
decisions.reason: The brain dump named how-to and why, but when asked directly the author chose to leave them out. The README and design docs keep that content.

decisions.decision: The guide and the README coexist, and the README gains a link
decisions.rejected: Slimming the README by moving its long-form content into the guide
decisions.reason: The smallest diff. The facts both documents repeat are guarded by the coverage tests rather than removed from one of them.

decisions.decision: Ride-along samples are verbatim copies of tests/golden/<leg>.txt, asserted byte for byte
decisions.rejected: Illustrative, abbreviated samples that are not tested
decisions.reason: Waybill output is the part most likely to change. Re-blessing a golden then fails the guide test until the guide is updated too.

decisions.decision: A folder of chapters in docs/guide/
decisions.rejected: One docs/GUIDE.md capped at about 600 lines; one file with no cap
decisions.reason: The author chose room to grow over a single scroll. The link-resolution test covers the extra links that chapters add.

decisions.decision: Repoint the help card's pointer at docs/guide/ and amend add-help-card's spec delta to match
decisions.rejected: Naming both the guide and README.md on one line, which leaves the spec unchanged; leaving the card alone
decisions.reason: The author wants the guide to be the card's next step and the governing requirement to say so plainly, rather than working around the requirement's wording.

decisions.rejected: Leaving prerequisites in the README only
decisions.reason: A newcomer riding along will reach a leg whose carrier isn't installed, and the reference is where they will look.

decisions.decision: The help-card repoint, the spec amendment and the prerequisites table are MVP, not Full
decisions.rejected: Keeping them in the Full tier (the pre-critic plan)
decisions.reason: The scope-creep critic found that goals G4 and G5 and three success criteria require them, so shipping MVP only would fail 3 of the 13 criteria. The goals won.

decisions.decision: Export REQUIRED and OPTIONAL from src/bookings.js, and parse flags from run(["--help"])
decisions.rejected: The pre-critic plan left the test's source for these lists unstated, which in practice means copying them into the test
decisions.reason: Found by the hidden-dependency and success-criteria critics. A hard-coded list passes when a new key or flag lands, which defeats a coverage test.

decisions.decision: Waybill samples live in ```waybill fences; that info string is what the golden test selects on
decisions.rejected: Matching every fenced block, which the pre-critic plan left unspecified
decisions.reason: The ride-along also has shell-command fences. Without a marker, the test either fails on those or quietly skips a drifting sample.

decisions.decision: The help pointer reads "Ride-along, glossary and reference: docs/guide/ in the waybill repo"
decisions.rejected: A bare docs/guide/, or keeping the old line's promise of overlays and environment variables
decisions.reason: help runs in the user's own repo, so a bare path points at a folder that isn't there, and the guide deliberately has no overlay how-to. 67 columns, under the 80-column cap.

phases.title: Waybill Guide
phases.notes: Test-first: tests/guide.test.js (registered in tests/index.js), exporting REQUIRED and OPTIONAL from src/bookings.js, then the four docs/guide/ files (samples in ```waybill fences), the README link, the help-card pointer with a re-blessed golden (UPDATE_GOLDEN=1), and the add-help-card spec and design amendment. Run node --test tests/ on Node 22 and 26 by hand.
